problem: The arithmetic is right, but the closing sentence mislabels the quantity. With the formula used, the intake-charge exhaust fraction is x = (1.80 − 0.04)/(12.0 − 0.04) = 1.76/11.96 = 14.7% by mass. The chapter's formula, which divides by (CO₂ exhaust − CO₂ intake) instead of (CO₂ exhaust − CO₂ ambient), gives x/(1 − x) = 17.3%, i.e. the mass of recirculated exhaust per 100 parts of fresh air. Calling 17.3% 'the EGR percentage of the intake charge' is wrong, and a student who writes that in an exam is wrong.
fix: Keep the formula (it is the one used in most lab manuals) and keep 17.3%, but correct the meaning: 'The CO₂ formula gives the recirculated exhaust mass per 100 parts of fresh air, 17.3%. As a fraction of the intake charge itself the exhaust is (1.76 ÷ 11.96) × 100 = 14.7%.' Reword the last exam trap to say the formula divides by the intake CO₂, so the answer is an exhaust-to-fresh-air ratio, not a fraction of the exhaust flow.

problem: Unit slip. Section 2 gives the window as ±0.3 in air-fuel ratio, but the trap says the TWC needs 'λ within about ±0.3 of stoichiometric'. A λ tolerance of ±0.3 means AFR from about 10.3 to 19.1, which is outside the catalyst window completely; the two statements also contradict each other.
fix: Use one unit. Write: 'The TWC needs λ within about ±0.01 of 1 (roughly ±0.2 in air-fuel ratio around 14.7:1); spare O₂ blocks NOx reduction and excess fuel blocks CO and HC oxidation.'

problem: The window is given only as 'about ±0.3 air-fuel ratio'. The width differs between sources and is clearest as a λ band; stated alone as an AFR tolerance it is on the wide side and does not match the ±0.3 λ slip in the traps.
fix: Give the band in λ as well: 'The window is narrow, about λ = 0.99 to 1.00 (a few tenths of an air-fuel ratio around 14.7:1 for petrol).'

problem: A lean-burn petrol engine is not normally given a DPF; its NOx route is an LNT (or SCR), and the particulate filter that appears on modern direct-injection petrol cars is a gasoline particulate filter, which the table does not mention. As written, students will think a diesel-style DPF is standard on lean petrol.
fix: Change the row to 'Lean-burn petrol | Lean | LNT (NOx storage catalyst), or SCR; add a gasoline particulate filter (GPF) where PM is regulated'.
